channel.title: Philosophy, Programs, and Prompts
channel.description: Everyone is talking about AI. But who is actually worth listening to, and not just pushing their own agenda? Carl is a veteran software engineer who has spent decades actually building systems. Casey is an analytic philosopher with ten years of ontology development. Neither has a book to sell or is funded by an AI thinktank. Together, they do something rare: think carefully and talk honestly about what AI is, what it can (and can’t) do, and how we should live in a world increasingly shaped by AI.

item.title: Inside the TESC Ideologies: Transhumanism, Extropianism, Singularitarianism & Cosmism
item.description: In this episode of Philosophy, Programs, and Prompts, Casey Hart( @OntologyExplained ) and Carl Brown( @InternetOfBugs ) dive into the "TESC" side of the TESCREAL framework—unpacking Transhumanism, Extropianism, Singularitarianism, and Cosmism.Following their breakdown of the "REAL" movements (Rationalism, Effective Altruism, and Longtermism), the hosts explore how sci-fi literature, mythological archetypes, and religious impulses continue to shape Silicon Valley's tech elite. From Vernor Vinge’s early singularity concepts and Ray Kurzweil’s exponential curves to Max More’s fight against entropy and the Russian roots of Cosmism, Casey and Carl examine the ideological machinery driving modern AI accelerationism.They also confront the darker historical shadows intertwined with these techno-optimist philosophies—including eugenics, population decline anxieties, digital post-humanism, and the bizarre, high-stakes promises of cryonics.### Referenced Sources & Reading List// Julian Huxley – New Bottles for New Wine (1957) https://archive.org/details/newbottlesfornew0000unsehttps://archive.org/details/NewBottlesForNewWine/page/n5/mode/2up// Ray Kurzweil – The Singularity Is Near: When Humans Transcend Biology (2005) https://www.kurzweilai.net/the-singularity-is-near-when-humans-transcend-biologyhttps://dn790006.ca.archive.org/0/items/kurzweil-ray-the-singularity-is-near/Kurzweil%2C%20Ray%20-%20The%20Singularity%20Is%20Near.pdf // Max More – The Principles of Extropy / Extropian Principles https://extropy.org/principles.htm// Nick Bostrom – A History of Transhumanist Thought (2005) https://nickbostrom.com/papers/history.pdfhttps://nickbostrom.com/papers/a-history-of-transhumanist-thought/// Aldous Huxley – Brave New World (1932) https://openlibrary.org/books/OL49337505M/Brave_New_World// Ray Bradbury – The Illustrated Man (1951) https://www.harpercollins.com/products/the-illustrated-man-ray-bradbury// Dennis E. item.title: Getting REAL: Rationalism Effective Altruism Longtermism
item.description: In this episode of Philosophy Programs and Prompts, Casey Hart ( @OntologyExplained ) and Carl Brown( @InternetOfBugs ) take a deep dive into the "R-E-A-L" half of the TESCREAL acronym (coined by Émile P. Torres and Timnit Gebru): Rationalism, Effective Altruism, and Longtermism.Starting with the intellectual roots of online rationalism—from LessWrong and Eliezer Yudkowsky to the Center for Applied Rationality (CFAR)—the conversation traces how reasonable ideas about cognitive bias, decision theory, and clear thinking evolved into a distinct subculture closely tied to Silicon Valley and artificial intelligence. Next, Casey and Carl examine Effective Altruism, tracing its trajectory from Peter Singer’s thought experiments and GiveWell’s charity evaluations to the "earning to give" ethos that paved the way for figures like Sam Bankman-Fried (FTX). Finally, they analyze Longtermism, addressing how utilitarian maximization can lead to thought experiments involving 10^20 virtual human beings, existential risk prioritizations (from pandemics to AI extinction), and moral blind spots regarding people living in the present.Subscribe for more grounded, hype-free takes from two real humans who know the tech!More info about Casey:https://CaseyHart.com/More info about Carl:https://InternetOfBugs.com/// Sources:* "Famine, Affluence, and Morality" (1972) by Peter Singerhttps://www.abebooks.com/9780190219208/Famine-Affluence-Morality-Singer-Peter-0190219203/plp * "The Most Good You Can Do" (2015) by Peter Singerhttps://www.abebooks.com/Good-Effective-Altruism-Changing-Ideas-Living/32491397359/bd * "Winners Take All: The Elite Charade of Changing the World" (2018) by Anand Giridharadashttps://www.abebooks.com/Winners-Take-Elite-Charade-Changing-World/32517761692/bd * The TESCREAL Acronym — Coined by Dr. Timnit Gebru and Émile P. item.title: Is Claude Conscious or just a Tool? | Ep 15
item.description:
In this episode of *Philosophy, Programs, and Prompts*, hosts Casey Hart ( @OntologyExplained ) and Carl Brown ( @InternetOfBugs ) dive into the strange intersection of theology, tech hype, and AI ethics. Anthropic recently updated its terms of service to forbid "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior" toward its models—effectively banning users from "torturing" Claude. But are large language models actually capable of feeling pain, or are we just projecting humanity into statistical matrix math?Casey and Carl explore Anthropic's lobbying efforts aimed at the Catholic Church and other religious leaders, the Pope’s encyclical addressing machine intelligence and human art, and the philosophical absurdity of two recent papers claiming to map "functional pain" and "well-being" onto LLM vector spaces. Along the way, they unpack a viral GitHub "torture chamber" experiment, why adding a "constipation vector" breaks an LLM just as easily as pain, and why current AI models remain miles away from genuine sentience.

item.title: Alignment Problem Part 2 - Taking it Seriously
item.description: Can the AI "alignment problem" actually be defined, or is it fundamentally flawed from the start? In this episode of Philosophy, Programs, and Prompts, Casey Hart( @OntologyExplained ) and Carl Brown( @InternetOfBugs ) set aside bad-faith doomer rhetoric and corporate marketing moats to examine the core arguments behind AI alignment in good faith.Casey argues that grappling with alignment acts as a conceptual gateway into foundational questions of ethics, paternalism, and what constitutes the "good life". Meanwhile, Carl pushes back from an engineering and practical standpoint, arguing that true alignment with humanity—which is notoriously misaligned with itself—is a distraction from pressing real-world issues like environmental degradation, social media algorithms, legal accountability, and building practical systems we can control.Together, they dissect the mechanics of Coherent Extrapolated Volition (CEV), Isaac Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics, Nick Bostrom's orthogonality thesis, and the practical limits of guardrails, kill switches, and machine interpretability.---Links & Resources Mentioned:// Eliezer Yudkowsky – Coherent Extrapolated Volition (2004):https://intelligence.org/files/CEV.pdf// Nick Bostrom – Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies (2014): Referenced for the Orthogonality Thesis (01:06:44) and the Paperclip Maximizer https://global.oup.com/academic/product/superintelligence-9780199678112?cc=us&lang=enhttps://rudyct.com/ai/Superintelligence%20Paths,%20Dangers,%20Strategies%20%28Nick%20Bostrom%292014.pdf---CHAPTERS:00:00 - item.title: Debunking AI Doom: Why Existential Risk Arguments Fall Apart | Ep 12
item.description:
Is artificial intelligence really on track to wipe out humanity by 2050, or are the most prominent doom arguments fundamentally flawed? In this episode of Philosophy Programs and Prompts, Casey Hart( @OntologyExplained ) and Carl Brown( @InternetOfBugs ) break down the core premises behind AI existential risk (x-risk). From Bostrom-style superintelligence scenarios and recursive self-improvement (RSI) to "hockey stick" benchmark progress and the appeal to expert anxiety, Casey and Carl analyze where the logic holds up—and where it jumps the rails. More importantly, they discuss why hyper-focusing on apocalyptic sci-fi scenarios distracts the public and regulators from the very real, immediate harms AI systems are causing right now: cyber vulnerabilities, military reliance on hallucinated outputs, non-consensual deepfakes, and corporate regulatory capture.

item.description: In this episode of Philosophy, Programs, and Prompts, Casey Hart ( @OntologyExplained ) and Carl Brown( @InternetOfBugs ) break down the growing backlash against AI in software development. item.title: Artificial Super Intelligence
item.description: "We're not going to be able to kill it. We're not going to be able to stop it..."Welcome back to Philosophy Programs and Prompts. In this episode, Casey and Carl take a hard, realistic look at Artificial Super Intelligence (ASI). While tech founders and doomer non-profits stand to gain massive clicks and capital by pitching a looming, god-like AI deity, the actual engineering constraints paint a completely different story. We deconstruct the core arguments driving the ASI panic: from the flawed chess masters analogy to the physical impossibility of infinite recursive self-improvement. More importantly, we discuss how abstract "human extinction" narratives are actively distracting us from real, pressing AI harms happening right now—including deepfakes, non-consensual intimate imagery, and mental health crises. Grounded in real-world software engineering and academic philosophy, we explore why an AI god won't fix global resource allocation, and why power disparities will likely remain human-led endeavors.
